info.title: Nscale Inference API
info.description:
Serverless inference and model discovery. Use a model ID returned by GET /v1/models. Modalities, tool use and generation options depend on the selected model. Inference requests have a 32 MiB body limit. Unknown JSON fields may be ignored; sending an undocumented field does not guarantee support for it.

post.description: Returns a chat completion as JSON, or server-sent events when stream is true. Non-streaming responses may contain a partial completion and may omit logprobs, refusal and stop_reason. A streaming request may end with an error event without a [DONE] marker if no response data arrives before the idle timeout.

OrganizationId.description: Selects the caller's public-cloud organization. Required when the caller belongs to multiple public-cloud organizations and the URL does not select an organization; omission then returns 400. With one public-cloud organization, omission selects it automatically. An explicitly supplied value, including an empty value, that is not one of the caller's public-cloud organizations returns 403. On /organizations/{organization_id}/endpoints, the path organization_id takes precedence over this header.

RequestId.description: Optional correlation identifier. Use the X-Request-Id returned in the response when contacting support. The response ID may differ from this value. Supplying this header does not make a request idempotent.

BearerAuth.description: Nscale bearer token supplied in the Authorization header.

AnthropicMessageRequest.description: Supported Messages request fields. Tool results support text only; is_error and non-text results do not affect the response. Only custom function tools are supported; disable_parallel_tool_use does not control parallel tool calls. Cache controls, metadata, top_k, hosted tools, thinking controls and reasoning-history blocks are not supported. Unknown fields may be accepted and ignored.

model.description: Model ID from GET /v1/models. Capabilities depend on the selected model.

tool_choice.description: Defaults to none when tools are omitted or empty; defaults to auto when tools are supplied.

reasoning_effort.description: Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Currently supported values are none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max. Reducing reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used on reasoning in a response. Note that 'max' is specific to the DeepSeek V4 series and is not part of the standard OpenAI API specification.

truncation_side.description: Which side to truncate from when truncate_prompt_tokens is active. 'right' keeps the first N tokens. 'left' keeps the last N tokens.

logprob_token_ids.description: Specific vocab token IDs to return logprobs for at each generated position, in addition to the sampled token. More efficient than `top_logprobs=-1` when only a small fixed label set is needed (e.g. multilabel scoring where each label corresponds to a known vocab id). When set, this explicit token selection takes precedence over the natural top-k selected by `top_logprobs`. Requires `logprobs=True`.

echo.description: If true, the new message will be prepended with the last message if they belong to the same role.

add_generation_prompt.description: If true, the generation prompt will be added to the chat template. This is a parameter used by chat template in tokenizer config of the model.

continue_final_message.description: If this is set, the chat will be formatted so that the final message in the chat is open-ended, without any EOS tokens. The model will continue this message rather than starting a new one. This allows you to "prefill" part of the model's response for it. Cannot be used at the same time as `add_generation_prompt`.

add_special_tokens.description: If true, special tokens (e.g. BOS) will be added to the prompt on top of what is added by the chat template. For most models, the chat template takes care of adding the special tokens so this should be set to false (as is the default).

documents.description: A list of dicts representing documents that will be accessible to the model if it is performing RAG (retrieval-augmented generation). If the template does not support RAG, this argument will have no effect. We recommend that each document should be a dict containing "title" and "text" keys.

chat_template.description: Jinja template for formatting conversation messages. Availability depends on the selected model.

chat_template_kwargs.description: Additional keyword args to pass to the template renderer. Will be accessible by the chat template.

media_io_kwargs.description: Model-specific options for reading image, audio and video inputs, keyed by modality.

mm_processor_kwargs.description: Model-specific options for processing image, audio and video inputs.

priority.description: Scheduling priority; lower values are handled first. Non-zero priorities require support from the selected model.

request_id.description: Identifier for the generation request. Generated when omitted. This is separate from the X-Request-Id HTTP correlation header.

session_id.description: Stable session identity shared by related requests. Unlike request_id, this value is expected to remain stable across multiple requests in the same conversation or agent session.

return_tokens_as_token_ids.description: If specified with 'logprobs', tokens are represented  as strings of the form 'token_id:{token_id}' so that tokens that are not JSON-encodable can be identified.

return_token_ids.description: If specified, the result will include token IDs alongside the generated text. In streaming mode, prompt_token_ids is included only in the first chunk, and token_ids contains the delta tokens for each chunk. This is useful for debugging or when you need to map generated text back to input tokens.

return_prompt_text.description: If true, the response will include ``prompt_text`` containing the prompt string produced by chat templating. In streaming mode it is sent only on the first chunk. This is useful for inspecting exactly what was fed into the model.

cache_salt.description: If specified, the prefix cache will be salted with the provided string to prevent an attacker to guess prompts in multi-user environments. The salt should be random, protected from access by 3rd parties, and long enough to be unpredictable (e.g., 43 characters base64-encoded, corresponding to 256 bit).

This feature can detect such behavior and terminate early, saving time and tokens.

frequency_penalty.description: The frequency penalty that was used to penalize new tokens based on their frequency in the text so far.

request_id.description: Identifier for the generation request. Generated when omitted. This is separate from the X-Request-Id HTTP correlation header.

session_id.description: Stable session identity shared by related requests. Unlike request_id, this value is expected to remain stable across multiple requests in the same conversation or agent session.

media_io_kwargs.description: Model-specific options for reading image, audio and video inputs, keyed by modality.

mm_processor_kwargs.description: Model-specific options for processing image, audio and video inputs.

priority.description: Scheduling priority; lower values are handled first. Non-zero priorities require support from the selected model.

cache_salt.description: If specified, the prefix cache will be salted with the provided string to prevent an attacker to guess prompts in multi-user environments. The salt should be random, protected from access by 3rd parties, and long enough to be unpredictable (e.g., 43 characters base64-encoded, corresponding to 256 bit).

enable_response_messages.description: Dictates whether or not to return messages as part of the response object. Currently only supported for non-background.

vllm_xargs.description: Additional request parameters with (list of) string or numeric values, used by custom extensions.

chat_template_kwargs.description: Additional keyword args to pass to the chat template renderer. Will be accessible by the template.

presence_penalty.description: The presence penalty that was used to penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far.

frequency_penalty.description: The frequency penalty that was used to penalize new tokens based on their frequency in the text so far.

input_messages.description: If enable_response_messages, we can show raw token input to model.

output_messages.description: If enable_response_messages, we can show raw token output of model.

input.description: USD per million input tokens; zero for image models.

output.description: USD per million output tokens, or the pixel rate for image models.

cached_input_read.description: USD per million cached input tokens. Omitted when no cached rate is available.
